name: Emperor-system fascism
summary: Emperor-system fascism is the account, developed by Japanese Marxist historians and Masao Maruyama, of wartime Japan as a fascism built on the emperor system and the kokutai myth: sovereignty in a divine emperor, an ultranationalist, militarist, expansionist state, repression of liberal and left thought, anti-communism and total mobilisation, run from above by the military and bureaucracy rather than by a mass party. The sources make no claims on economy, gender, ecology or most social questions.
scope: The wartime Japanese state and ideology of c.1931-1945 as the concept named 'emperor-system fascism' / 'Japanese fascism' (Maruyama's 'Japanese fascism', the Marxist 'emperor-system fascism') describes them, as set out in Young (2017), Tansman's The Culture of Japanese Fascism (2009) and Munderloh's thesis following Maruyama. Excluded: the kokutai doctrine as its own subject (Kokkashugi, Japanese nationalism), European fascism, and the critics' view (Tsuneki), which is used only to show the concept exists; Maruyama's own essay could not be opened.

keyFigures.role: Political theorist who defined 'Japanese fascism' as fascism from below and from above
keyFigures.quote: Maruyama Masao challenged the Marxian interpretation of fascism

suppress-opposition.rationale: The wartime state's record was a crackdown on liberal and left-wing thought, mass arrests of communists, the end of party cabinets from 1932 and, under the Peace Preservation Law, special-police arrests of 'thought criminals'.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Military aggression abroad (Manchuria from 1931, China, the Pacific War) is the defining external act of the regime, summed up by the Marxists as 'military aggression abroad; political repression at home'.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: The army was unleashed across Asia to serve the interests of financial-industrial combines and a Japanese-led New Order, not defence alone.

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: The regime initiated the Manchurian Incident and later wars of conquest, a record that could not coexist with this view.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: The regime made client states (Manchukuo) and imposed a Japanese-led New Order in Asia rather than staying out of other countries' affairs.

conscription.rationale: Universal conscription was a pillar of the system and its indoctrination: nearly all young men passed through the army or its reservist associations.

patriotic-education.rationale: Compulsory education was shaped by the Imperial Rescript on Education to instil loyalty to the emperor and patriotism, with kokutai clarification written into the curriculum.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The state-backed seinendan youth associations gave males from school-leaving age to conscription age physical and spiritual training, spread military values and prepared them for service.

total-state.rationale: The record is mobilisation for total war, thought control and 'radical statism', with the state treated as omnipotent and individuals formed into a collective body.

military-superiority.rationale: The regime's hyper-militarism and glorification of the military, with the army kept independent of the cabinet and a military build-up, aimed at military dominance in Asia.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: The army and its patrons tolerated and exploited assassinations and coup attempts by young officers and the radical right, and used war as a political instrument.

party-controls-media.rationale: From the Manchurian Incident the press was brought under military and state control and became a propaganda outlet, with instructions on what could be published.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The fascist turn rested on authoritarian control and suspension of the rule of law, and the Peace Preservation Law was enlarged by emergency imperial edict to enlarge police powers against internal enemies.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Peace Preservation Law made endangering the kokutai illegal and was used against communists and other radicals, while parties dissolved themselves under pressure.

democracy-best.rationale: Record: party cabinets ended in 1932, the Diet and parties lost power, and the remaining liberal and democratic tendencies were eradicated.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Meiji order vested sovereignty in the emperor, and the Diet's role was reduced further as the military and bureaucracy ruled.

defeat-communism.rationale: The 'red peril' is one of the four defining elements of fascism in Japan in Young's account, expressed in an empire-wide anti-communist police state.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Asianism was the 'loadstar for regional autarky', and Manchukuo and the New Order were organised as an economic bloc under Japanese control.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Manchukuo and the Co-prosperity Sphere gave client states nominal sovereignty under Japanese political control and a Japanese-led alliance.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Hyper-militarism and the army's political role are central to the regime, which could not abolish its armed forces.

arms-reduction.rationale: The regime built up military force and prepared the nation for total war, the opposite of keeping armaments at a minimum.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: The Kwantung Army held Manchukuo and the army occupied and ruled conquered territory as the regime's policy.

nation-first.rationale: Ultranationalism and expansion in the name of Japanese leadership of Asia put national aims ahead of the international order, which the regime rejected.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The ideology rests on the divine origins of the imperial line and the divinity of the emperor, and a revitalised cult of imperial rule.

leader-cult.rationale: The archaic identification of nation with emperor and the cult of imperial rule were central to the ideology.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The ideology is built on the unbroken imperial line descended from the gods.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The divine descent of the hereditary imperial line is the ideology's core, so abolishing hereditary rank contradicts it.

elective-rulers.rationale: Sovereignty belonged to the emperor, not the people, by divine descent, which excludes an elected head of state.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Sovereignty belonged to the emperor by descent, not to the people, so no popular election of the head of state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The emperor system vested sovereignty in the emperor rather than the people and made people submissive through inculcation and force.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Kokutai presented the unbroken imperial line from the gods as the basis of national identity, paired with ancient myth to create the illusion of a continuous tradition.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: The ideological background is described as including the ethnic divinity and superiority of the Japanese people and a divine world mission.

national-mission.rationale: The ideology held a divine world mission for the Japanese state and global imperial rule under the emperor.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The kokutai ideology defined Japan as of 'unrivaled superiority', and fascism in Japan acted in the name of dominating peoples of 'poorer bloodline' abroad.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The ideology rejected individualism and liberalism and demanded the individual's devotion and sacrifice to state, nation or lineage.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The ideology demanded obedience and sacrifice of the individual to the state, nation or lineage and valued collectivist loyalty.

person-over-state.rationale: It demanded devotion and sacrifice of the individual to the state and formed individuals into a collective body.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Kokutai clarification was written into the curriculum, using the Kojiki and Nihongi paired with Meiji examples to teach the national past.

separate-church-state.rationale: The state ideology was built on the Shinto creation story and the divinity of the emperor (radical Shinto ultranationalism).

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The ideology presented a direct, spiritual link between emperor and people that made representative institutions unnecessary.

national-rebirth.rationale: The radical wing sought a 'Showa restoration' to renovate and revitalise the imperial state and a spiritual reformation of Japan.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Kokutai summed up the virtues that defined what it meant to be Japanese, and the ideology used heritage to bind the nation.
